standard.title: Shape ideas with media technologies
standard.description: develop media production skills by exploring ways of shaping ideas using media technologies, images, sounds, text and/or interactive elements
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can capture and organise media elements and experiment with how changes affect meaning. They can apply basic production skills. They have not yet systematically explored how specific production techniques (suspense, genre conventions, Foley sound) shape meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop media production skills by exploring ways of shaping ideas using media technologies, images, sounds, text and/or interactive elements.

nodes.label: Techniques that shape meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe at least two production techniques (e.g. suspense through editing, genre conventions, Foley sound creation) and explain how each shapes meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one technique used in an existing media work (e.g. how colour and editing create suspense in a film genre clip) and explain how it shapes the audience's experience.
nodes.typical_width: Explore how colour, shot type and editing create suspense and genre meaning; investigate how news story conventions and video game conventions communicate differently from narrative; explore how sound effects and music change mood and meaning.
wider: Investigate how the conventions of a news story or video game communicate meaning — examining speech bubble text, headlines and framing choices to understand how form shapes audience expectations
Explore how colour, shot type and editing techniques signal film genre — comparing two clips from different genres and identifying the techniques that create genre recognition
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding specific production techniques and their effects is the prerequisite for deliberately applying them — without this, exploration of media technologies is random rather than purposeful.

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints questions to scaffold technique analysis: 'Where is the suspense happening in this work, and how do I know?' This builds transferable analytical skills.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least two production techniques in existing media works
Student can explain how each technique shapes meaning or audience experience

nodes.label: Exploring and experimenting
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can experiment with media technologies to apply and modify production techniques — using Viewpoints questions to evaluate what changes when techniques are altered.
nodes.minimum_width: Experiment with at least one production technique (e.g. create Foley sounds using found objects, or modify the sound effects on an image sequence) and describe how the change affects the mood or meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment across multiple techniques — Foley sound creation, storyboarding and rearranging sequences, zooming in/out, adding text and sound to images, reviewing and selecting captured images; use Viewpoints questions to evaluate experiments: 'In what ways does the meaning change when I manipulate the sound effects?'
wider: Create multiple soundscapes for the same image sequence using different materials and sound types (Foley, voice, recorded sounds) — comparing how each soundscape changes the mood and meaning, and selecting the most effective approach

Experiment with digital and analog storyboarding as a planning tool — create a storyboard for a short film or comic strip, rearrange the boards to create different narrative meanings, and test audience responses

response_modes.reason: Build students' repertoire of experimenting strategies — Foley, storyboard rearrangement, image review, sound-image combination. A broader repertoire means more informed production choices in later work.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of production experimentation available at Y3-4 (Foley sound, storyboarding, image review, genre experimentation) is genuinely rich — students who explore across multiple techniques develop much stronger production decision-making.
success_criteria: Student experiments with at least one production technique using media technologies
Student uses Viewpoints questions or equivalent reflection to evaluate what changed and why
